messages:
Maria: quick sanity check — i'm adding a KMS decrypt grant for the eks operator service account (namespace: monitoring, sa: operator). gonna apply via our terraform module, but wanted to make sure the principal + conditions are right before i push the PR :thinking_face:

Maria: current plan is to have a aws_kms_grant resource with 'GranteePrincipal' set to the role created by IRSA (the OIDC role for the service account). terraform snippet below (simplified):
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "monitoring_operator_irsa" {
  name = "monitoring-operator-irsa-${var.cluster_name}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_sa.json
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "operator_decrypt" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.app.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.monitoring_operator_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt"]
}
```

Maria: any obvious red flags? i'm trying to avoid giving full decrypt to broader principals or tying to svcacct annotations incorrectly.

Jake: ping @Maria — couple quick things:
- you probably want grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.monitoring_operator_irsa.unique_id (or the role ARN is fine, but double-check the docs for grant principal type).
- check that KMS key policy allows grants from AWS principals (we've got a restrictive key policy on the app key). if the key policy forbids external grants, the grant will 403 even if IAM allows it.

Sam: also watch the SourceAccount/SourceArn condition if you add it. for IRSA the SourceArn should be the role arn or the federated principal? we've done in the past:
- condition aws:PrincipalTag/eks:cluster-name or aws:SourceArn = arn:aws:sts::ACCOUNT:assumed-role/ROLE_NAME/sa_NAMESPACE.SA_NAME

Sam: TL;DR: prefer adding a condition on the grant that ties it to the specific role/session so the grant can't be abused by other principals.

Maria: aha, thanks. do you have an example of the grant with a condition? i was going to rely on the IAM role + key policy but adding condition seems safer.

devops-jen: we have a pattern in infra-modules for this. example we've used (terraform + json policy blob):
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "operator_decrypt" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.app.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.monitoring_operator_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt"]
  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = {
      "aws:eks:sa" = "monitoring/operator"
    }
  }
}

# if using explicit condition on key policy side:
# "Condition": { "StringLike": { "aws:SourceArn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/*/sa_monitoring.operator" }}
```

devops-jen: note though: encryption_context_subset only works if the client passes that encryption context when calling decrypt. many SDKs don't set it automatically. more robust is SourceArn-based condition.

Maria: good call. our operator doesn't set encryption context on decrypt calls. we'll do SourceArn condition on the key policy + create grant for the role.

Jake: small nit: avoid using wildcard in SourceArn if you can — the exact assumed-role session name pattern for IRSA is usually `assumed-role/<role-name>/<namespace>.<serviceaccount>`. so something like:
`arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/monitoring-operator-irsa/monitoring.operator`

Maria: got it. i'll update the PR to add a key policy statement allowing kms:Decrypt to the role arn but constrained by SourceArn exact match, then create a grant in TF.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: terraform plan for branch feature/monitoring/kms-grant at commit 8f3a2e2 — Plan: 2 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. (checks passed) :white_check_mark:

Maria: pushing PR in a sec — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123 (contains key policy + grant + module usage). would appreciate a quick review, especially from @devops-jen and @Sam for policy condition phrasing.

Sam: looking now, one more thought: if the role is recreated (name change) the grant might orphan. consider using key policy allowance as the primary control and treat aws_kms_grant as convenience for management, not required for access.

Maria: makes sense. I'll keep both but ensure the key policy is the canonical access rule. thanks y'all :pray: 

Jake: LGTM once devops-jen signs off on condition wording.

devops-jen: quick review done, left one inline comment about using the account ID from vars rather than numeric literal. otherwise 👍

Maria: merged and will monitor. thanks all :rocket:
